_about: Hero vehicle parameters. hue_ranges are HSV [lo,hi] pairs of the PAINT; attach_dark_max_v/_s attach the car's dark part to it (0 = the paint covers the whole car, which is the case for a car painted at both ends). open_kernel removes specks; close_kernel joins the body's halves; min_area rejects smaller things. Re-record the front/rear template afterwards and CHECK corr(right,left) is negative.
_measured: Measured on the real car. The paint (yellow nose) is all a colour mask can see: H 24..33, S 93..138, V 115..211, 693 px level, position jitter +-0.14 px. The cabin is found by asking WHICH WAY from the paint it is dark, not by looking for dark pixels: beside the paint, right=78 (the cabin) against above 181, left 178, below 173 and a road at 186 - a 20:1 separation that did not move with the threshold (20, 30 and 40 levels gave the same answer). The union is kept to a corridor the width of the paint so the car's shadow is not absorbed; 16 rays at 22.5 degrees, because four axis-aligned boxes were found by a rotation sweep to work only when the car is level (at 15/30/45 degrees the cabin is beyond a corner and the mask fell back to the paint alone). The corridor's half width is 0.5*sqrt(area) rather than half the bounding box diagonal, which grows when the car is turned and swallowed the road: 12,586 px against the car's 5,495. Level and live: 79x31, area 2,101-2,923 px, elongation 2.14-2.99, centre (472.6,427.4) instead of the nose's (443,427). The front is the painted end - a fact about this car, applied only when the paint covers under 80% of the car's length, because a car painted end to end has no painted end to point at. Live after the direction fix: 40/40 frames point at the yellow nose (error median 9 degrees), frame to frame change median 0.1 degrees, and no 180 degree flips.
